guide.title: Haydn: String Quartet Op. 76 No. 3 'Emperor' – I. Allegro
guide.overview: This is a fast opening movement in C major, in three parts. Part 1 is repeated. Part 2 wanders through several keys. Section 3 is marked to be played faster ("più presto") on the second time through and brings the music home. Keys and chords here are estimated by computer, so treat them as a guide. Listen for the opening tune in Violin 1, and for how it comes back.

listening_points.headline: The opening tune in Violin 1
listening_points.text: Violin 1 plays the main theme in C major [m. 0-2]. The players move together, with chords under the tune. It starts loud, then drops to soft in [m. 1].

listening_points.headline: Louder, busier, still at home in C
listening_points.text: The music gets louder at [m. 3] and the lines become more independent. Violin 2 probably takes the tune briefly in [m. 5]. Sharp accents (marked fz) land in [m. 8-10].

listening_points.headline: A move up to G major
listening_points.text: At [m. 11] the key changes to G major. The computer estimates this key change. The lead is shared and unclear here, but Violin 1 probably has the tune from [m. 13].

listening_points.headline: A touch of D major, then back to G
listening_points.text: The key moves briefly to D major at [m. 20]. Accents (fz) stand out. At [m. 22] there is a very loud ff, and then the music drops at once to soft. By [m. 25] we are back in G major.

listening_points.headline: The dark, loud peak of Part 1
listening_points.text: The mood turns stormy in G minor. Minor keys sound darker. At [m. 30] the music is marked ff (very loud). The computer estimates this as the loudest and busiest point of the movement. Everyone plays together in block chords.

listening_points.headline: A sudden hush in E-flat major
listening_points.text: After the peak, the music drops to soft in a new key, E-flat major [m. 32-36]. Cello probably takes the tune briefly at [m. 33]. At [m. 36] the music is marked even softer, pp, and three instruments seem to play.

listening_points.headline: Closing Part 1 in G major
listening_points.text: G major returns at [m. 37], starting very soft. It turns loud at [m. 38]. The part ends softly in G major at [m. 44b]. Then it is repeated.

listening_points.headline: Part 2 begins in minor keys
listening_points.text: Part 2 opens in E minor [m. 45]. It then visits A minor [m. 53] and returns to E minor [m. 58]. Violin 1 leads clearly at the start. The mood is more restless and serious than before.

listening_points.headline: Bright B major and E major, then a hush
listening_points.text: The music moves to B major at [m. 60]. It goes soft, then lands in E major at [m. 64]. Many accents (fz) run through [m. 66-73], with busy independent lines. At [m. 74] it drops to soft.

listening_points.headline: Quiet E minor and a theme return
listening_points.text: The key turns to E minor and the music gets very soft [m. 76-77]. Then Violin 1 plays the main theme again, loud, at exactly the same pitch as the opening [m. 78-80]. The computer labels the key of these bars as E minor, but the tune is at the opening's pitch, and from [m. 80] the key is C major again.

listening_points.headline: Back in C major
listening_points.text: From [m. 80] the key is C major again. Violin 2 probably leads at [m. 83]. Accents return in [m. 86-88].

listening_points.headline: Through G major and back to C
listening_points.text: G major appears at [m. 90]. C major settles again at [m. 96]. The music is mostly loud, with a soft dip at [m. 94] and again at [m. 97]. At [m. 104] it goes soft, as if holding its breath.

listening_points.headline: Soft, with a turn to C minor (faster the second time)
listening_points.text: Section 3 starts soft [m. 105]. It is marked to go faster on the repeat. From [m. 108] to [m. 112] the key darkens into C minor. At [m. 113] C major comes back.

listening_points.headline: A loud push, then a soft ending
listening_points.text: The music turns loud at [m. 115] with Violin 1 probably on the melody. In the last bars it softens again. It ends quietly in C major at [m. 121b].

glossary.explanation: The home note and scale a passage feels built around. Major keys sound brighter. Minor keys sound darker.
A change from one key to another.
A main tune that you can recognise when it comes back.
All the instruments move together in the same rhythm, like a hymn.
One part has the tune. The others play support underneath.
Each instrument plays its own line at the same time.
A sudden sharp accent on a note.
Soft / very soft / loud / very loud.
